projectName: CPU-only PDF OCR to Piper TTS Audiobook Pipeline

services.name: Audiobook pipeline worker
services.description: A CPU-only batch pipeline that extracts PDF pages, runs OCR, cleans and segments text, synthesizes speech with Piper, and assembles audiobook audio.

questions.question: Which implementation language should the pipeline worker use?

options.label: Python
options.description: Strong ecosystem for PDF processing, OCR orchestration, audio assembly, and Piper integration.

options.label: C# (.NET)
options.description: Good for strongly typed cross-platform command-line applications.

options.label: JavaScript/TypeScript
options.description: Suitable when the pipeline is integrated with a Node.js service.

questions.rationale: Python provides the most practical CPU-only integrations for OCR and audio tooling.

questions.question: Which worker/runtime approach should organize the pipeline?

options.label: Python CLI with Typer
options.description: A focused, scriptable batch interface with clear commands and options.

options.label: Python CLI with argparse
options.description: Uses only the Python standard library for command-line parsing.

options.label: FastAPI job API
options.description: Exposes pipeline runs through an HTTP API, adding service overhead.

questions.rationale: A CLI keeps the first version CPU-only, local, and easy to automate.

questions.question: Describe any additional pipeline features, input constraints, or output preferences.
questions.recommendedChoice: Configurable OCR language and DPI; scanned and text PDFs; resumable page-level processing; chapter-aware WAV/MP3 output; progress and error reports.
questions.answer: Configurable OCR language and DPI; scanned and text PDFs; resumable page-level processing; chapter-aware WAV/MP3 output; progress and error reports.
questions.rationale: These capabilities make a CPU-only batch conversion reliable for typical books without requiring a hosted service.

questions.question: Which persistent stores should the pipeline use for inputs, intermediate artifacts, and generated audiobooks?

options.label: Blob Storage
options.description: Stores source PDFs, OCR text, intermediate manifests, and generated audio files.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Adds relational metadata and job tracking when a shared service is needed.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Use only ephemeral/local files and process state.

questions.rationale: The pipeline produces and serves document and media files; Blob Storage is the appropriate file store.

questions.question: Should users sign in for application API features?

options.label: No
options.description: Run the local batch pipeline without user accounts or an application API.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Require signed-in users for a future API or shared job service.

questions.rationale: The requested CPU-only pipeline is a local worker rather than a multi-user application.
